instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them in half. Put them in a pot, cover them with cold water and bring it to a boil over high. Turn the heat down and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily but they aren't falling apart. Drain them and spread them out to cool.
Meanwhile, start the dough. In a large bowl, mix the 2 cups flour, 3/4 tsp carom seeds, 3/4 tsp of the salt and 1/4 cup of the oil.

Rub the flour and oil together between your fingers for 3 to 4 minutes, until it looks like coarse crumbs. Squeeze a handful. It should hold its shape. Don't cut this short, or the crust won't be flaky.

Add 6 tbsp water a little at a time, mixing as you go, until it comes together into a stiff dough that still bends without cracking. It should feel firm, not soft and stretchy. Cover it and leave it for 30 minutes.
While the dough rests, mince 1 tbsp of the ginger, finely chop the green chili and chop 4 tbsp of the cilantro. Crumble the cooled potatoes into small pieces with your fingers. Don't mash them.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium and add the 3/4 tsp cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell toasty. Add the ginger, chili and the pinch of asafoetida and stir for 30 to 60 seconds, until the ginger smells fragrant.
Add the 1/2 cup peas and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the 3/4 tsp chili powder, 3/4 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp fennel and 1/2 tsp chaat masala. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring.

Add the potatoes and the last 1/2 tsp salt and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until the potatoes are coated and hot. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cilantro. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Spread the filling on a plate to cool and divide it into 10 even portions.
Knead the dough for a few seconds until it's smooth, divide it into 5 balls and keep them covered with a towel.
Rub a few drops of oil on the counter. Roll one ball into an oval about 8 inches long and 6 inches wide, then cut it across the middle into two half moons.
Take one half moon and brush water along the straight edge. Fold it into a cone, overlapping the wet edge by about 1/2 inch, and press the seam firmly to seal it.
Hold the cone open and fill it with one portion of filling, pressing it down. Brush water on the open edges and pinch them together firmly so there are no gaps. Set it on a tray under a towel.
Make the rest of the samosas the same way, so you have 10.

Pour the rest of the oil into a deep heavy pot. It should come no more than halfway up the sides. Heat it over medium low. You're heating it to about 300°F, so if you have a thermometer, clip it to the side. No thermometer? Drop in a pinch of dough: it's ready when tiny bubbles form around it and it takes a few seconds to float up.
Lower 5 samosas gently into the oil and fry them on low without moving them for 10 to 12 minutes, until the crust is firm but still pale.
Turn the heat up to medium. Turn them over and fry for another 3 to 4 minutes, turning now and then, until they're golden and crisp all over. Lift them onto a wire rack.
Turn the heat back to low for a couple of minutes, then fry the other 5 the same way.
Serve warm with the cilantro chutney and the tamarind chutney.
method_notes: Both read versions rub fat into flour with carom seeds and salt until it looks like breadcrumbs, knead a firm dough and rest it, fill cones of dough with a spiced potato and pea filling, and fry the samosas slowly on low heat so the crust turns flaky. Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) crumbles boiled potatoes into peas cooked with cumin seeds, ginger and green chili, seasons them with chili powder, garam masala, cumin, fennel and lemon or chaat masala, and fries on low for 10 to 12 minutes before turning up the heat to brown them. My Ginger Garlic Kitchen mashes the potato and adds pounded coriander and fennel seeds, cloves, cashews, raisins and amchur, makes 16 smaller samosas and also gives an air fryer method. This one follows the lead with chaat masala for the sour note and mild Kashmiri chili powder.
